mn: di-（二）+ lemma（命题）→ 两个选项摆在面前，都不好选 → 两难
“敌来吗？”——敌人来了，打还是逃？两难！
dilemma.ex: She faced a dilemma: take the job abroad or stay with her family.
dilemma.exZh: 她陷入两难：去国外工作，还是留在家人身边。
dilemma.col: face a dilemma 面临两难；moral dilemma 道德困境

mn: infra（在下面）+ structure（结构）→ 垫在城市下面撑着一切的结构 → 基础设施
infrastructure.ex: The country invested heavily in roads, railways and other infrastructure.
infrastructure.exZh: 该国在道路、铁路等基础设施上投入巨大。
infrastructure.col: transport infrastructure 交通基础设施

mn: re-（回）+ ven（来，同 venue 场馆、avenue 大街）→ 流回来的钱 → 收入
每个 venue（场馆）卖票，钱 re（回）到口袋 → revenue
revenue.ex: Advertising is the main source of revenue for most websites.
revenue.exZh: 广告是大多数网站的主要收入来源。
revenue.col: tax revenue 税收；generate revenue 创收

mn: legi（法律，同 legal 合法的）→ legal 的加长正式版 → 合法的、正当的
“立规矩它没的”——立了规矩它就没得说，合法正当
legitimate.ex: Workers have a legitimate right to ask for fair pay.
legitimate.exZh: 工人有正当权利要求公平的报酬。
legitimate.col: legitimate concern 合理的担忧；legitimate reason 正当理由
legitimate.fam: legitimacy n. 合法性；illegitimate adj. 不合法的
legitimate.zh: adj. 合法的；正当的；合理的

mn: con-（共同）+ sens（感觉，同 sense）→ 大家感觉一样 → 共识
consensus.ex: There is a growing consensus that smoking in public places should be banned.
consensus.exZh: 越来越多的人一致认为应禁止在公共场所吸烟。
consensus.col: reach a consensus 达成共识

mn: im-（进入）+ ple（填满，同 complete、plenty）→ 把计划填满、落到实处 → 实施
“硬扑了门”——政策硬扑进门，强制执行
implement.ex: The school will implement the new policy next term.
implement.exZh: 学校将在下学期实施新政策。
implement.col: implement a plan/policy 实施计划/政策
implement.zh: v. 实施；执行　n. 工具

mn: pro-（向前）+ found（底，同 foundation 地基、fundamental 根本的）→ 一直深入到底 → 深刻的
profound.ex: The internet has had a profound impact on how we learn.
profound.exZh: 互联网对我们的学习方式产生了深远影响。
profound.col: profound impact/effect 深远影响；profound change 深刻变化

mn: soph（智慧，同 philosophy 哲学 =“爱智慧”）→ 充满智慧的 → 精密的、老练的
“扫飞死题”——一扫就把难题打飞，真老练
sophisticated.ex: Modern cars are equipped with sophisticated computer systems.
sophisticated.exZh: 现代汽车配备了精密的计算机系统。
sophisticated.col: sophisticated technology 尖端技术；sophisticated taste 高雅的品味
sophisticated.zh: adj. 复杂精密的；老练的；见多识广的

mn: dis-（分开）+ rupt（断裂，同 bankrupt 破产、interrupt 打断）→ 打断、打散 → 扰乱
disrupt.ex: Heavy snow disrupted train services across the country.
disrupt.exZh: 大雪扰乱了全国的火车运行。
disrupt.col: disrupt traffic 扰乱交通；disruptive technology 颠覆性技术
disrupt.fam: disruption n. 中断；disruptive adj. 破坏性的

mn: surg（升起，同 source 源头——水从地下涌起）→ 猛地涌起 → 激增
surf（冲浪）的兄弟：浪头 surge 一下涌上来
surge.ex: There has been a surge in online shopping since 2020.
surge.col: a surge in demand 需求激增
surge.cf: 反义：plummet 暴跌（第 13 串）

mn: pro-（向前）+ spect（看，同 inspect 检查、spectator 观众）→ 向前看的 → 未来的、可能成为的
prospective.ex: The university holds open days for prospective students.
prospective.exZh: 大学为潜在的新生举办开放日。
prospective.col: prospective buyer/employer 潜在买家/未来雇主
prospective.zh: adj. 潜在的；未来的；预期的

mn: 来自拉丁语 robur（橡树）→ 壮得像橡树 → 强健的
“肉巴士”——一整车肌肉，壮实得很
robust.ex: The economy remained robust despite the crisis.
robust.exZh: 尽管有危机，经济依然稳健。
robust.col: robust growth 强劲增长；robust health 身体强健
robust.zh: adj. 强健的；稳健的；结实的

mn: off + set → 天平一边放亏损，另一边 set 上收益，正好 off 掉 → 抵消
offset.ex: Higher prices were offset by better quality.
offset.exZh: 价格上涨被更好的质量抵消了。
offset.col: offset the cost/losses 抵消成本/损失；carbon offset 碳抵消
offset.zh: v. 抵消；弥补（过去式同形）

mn: em-（进入）+ brace（手臂，同 bracelet 手镯）→ 揽入双臂 → 拥抱 → 欣然接受新事物
embrace.ex: Young people tend to embrace new technology quickly.
embrace.exZh: 年轻人往往很快接受新技术。
embrace.col: embrace change/an idea 拥抱变化/接受想法

mn: con-（共同）+ tend（伸展，同 extend）→ 大家一起伸手争 → 竞争；在辩论里争 → 主张
“肯藤的”——就是肯定这根藤是我的！坚持主张
contend.ex: Some scientists contend that the drug is unsafe.
contend.exZh: 一些科学家声称这种药不安全。
contend.col: contend with difficulties 对付困难
contend.cf: 同义：assert 断言（第 6 串）
contend.zh: v. 声称；主张；竞争；对付（with）

mn: “四顾特你”——四面八方都在盯着你看 → 被仔细审查
拉丁语 scruta 原指“碎布垃圾”→ 连垃圾堆都翻一遍 → 审查得极细
scrutiny.ex: The company's accounts came under close scrutiny.
scrutiny.exZh: 公司账目受到了严格审查。
scrutiny.col: under scrutiny 受到审查；public scrutiny 公众监督

mn: com-（加强）+ pel（推，同 propel 推进、expel 驱逐）→ 强力推着你相信 → 令人信服的
compelling.ex: She made a compelling argument for change.
compelling.exZh: 她提出了一个令人信服的变革理由。
compelling.col: compelling evidence 令人信服的证据；a compelling story 引人入胜的故事
compelling.zh: adj. 令人信服的；引人入胜的

mn: war（战争）+ rant（咆哮）→ 战场上大吼“我有命令！”→ 授权令
“我认它”——法官签了字，我就认它 → 搜查令
warrant.exZh: 这种情况需要立即采取行动。
warrant.col: search/arrest warrant 搜查令/逮捕令；warrant attention 值得关注
warrant.zh: n. 授权令；搜查令　v. 使有必要；值得

mn: integr（完整，同 integer 整数、integrate 整合）→ 人格完整无缺 → 正直、诚信
integrity.ex: He is a man of great integrity who never lies.
integrity.exZh: 他是一个从不说谎、非常正直的人。
integrity.col: academic integrity 学术诚信；personal integrity 个人品格

mn: 和 doom（审判、厄运）同源 → 下判断 → 认为、视为
“低眯”——低头眯眼看了看：我认为不行
deem.ex: The film was deemed unsuitable for children.
deem.exZh: 这部电影被认为不适合儿童观看。
deem.col: be deemed (to be) + adj./n. 被认为是……

mn: de-（加强）+ pict（画，同 picture）→ 画出来 → 描绘
depict.ex: The painting depicts a busy street in old Beijing.
depict.exZh: 这幅画描绘了老北京一条热闹的街道。
depict.col: depict sb. as… 把某人描绘成……

mn: 来自 curve（弯）：原指勒在马嘴下的弯链 → 勒住 → 抑制
“可不！”——可不能再这样了，赶紧遏制
curb.ex: The city introduced new rules to curb air pollution.
curb.exZh: 该市出台新规以控制空气污染。
curb.col: curb inflation/spending 抑制通胀/控制开支

mn: sub-（在下面）+ sid（坐，同 reside 居住、president 坐在前面的人）→ 坐在下面托底的钱 → 补贴
“杀不死弟”——有了补贴，弟弟饿不死
subsidy.ex: Farmers receive government subsidies to grow wheat.
subsidy.exZh: 农民种小麦可以得到政府补贴。
subsidy.col: government/farm subsidies 政府/农业补贴

mn: man（手，同 manual 手工的）+ date（给，同 donate 捐）→ 亲手交给你的命令 → 授权、强制
“慢点它！”——上头下了命令：给我慢点
mandate.ex: The law mandates that all new buildings have fire alarms.
mandate.exZh: 法律强制规定所有新建筑必须安装火警报警器。
mandate.col: a mandate to do 做某事的授权
mandate.zh: n. 授权；命令　v. 强制规定

mn: trans-（穿过）+ par（出现，同 appear）→ 光能穿过、里面一览无余 → 透明的
transparent.ex: The government promised a more transparent decision-making process.
transparent.exZh: 政府承诺决策过程更加透明。
transparent.zh: adj. 透明的；易懂的；坦率的

mn: vi（生命，同 vital 至关重要的、vivid 生动的）+ -able → 能活下去的 → 可行的
“外包”——外包出去也能活下来，这方案可行
viable.ex: Solar power is now a viable alternative to coal.
viable.exZh: 太阳能现已成为煤炭的可行替代品。
viable.col: a viable option/alternative 可行的选择

mn: sus（=sub 在下面）+ tain（握住，同 contain、maintain）→ 从下面托住 → 支撑、维持
sustain.ex: The planet cannot sustain this level of consumption.
sustain.exZh: 地球无法维持这种消费水平。
sustain.col: sustain growth 维持增长；sustain injuries 受伤
sustain.zh: v. 维持；支撑；遭受（损伤）

mn: un（不）+ pre（之前）+ ced（走，同 proceed）→ 之前没人走过的路 → 前所未有
unprecedented.ex: The pandemic caused unprecedented disruption to education.
unprecedented.exZh: 疫情给教育带来了前所未有的冲击。
unprecedented.col: on an unprecedented scale 以前所未有的规模

mn: pro-（向前）+ min（伸出，同 eminent 杰出的）→ 向前伸出来、一眼看见 → 突出的、著名的
prominent.ex: She is a prominent figure in the art world.
prominent.exZh: 她是艺术界的知名人物。
prominent.col: a prominent figure 知名人物；play a prominent role 起重要作用
prominent.zh: adj. 著名的；重要的；突出的

mn: in-（在里面）+ her（粘，同 adhere 粘附）→ 粘在里面拿不掉 → 固有的
in her ent →“在她(her)身体里”天生就有 → 固有的
inherent.exZh: 每项投资都有固有风险。
inherent.col: inherent risk 固有风险；be inherent in 是……固有的
inherent.cf: 近义：intrinsic 内在的（第 11 串）

mn: 古英语里和 food 同源 → 喂养 → 培养、收养
“否死的”——小树苗要好好培养，否则会死的
foster.ex: Reading to children fosters a love of books.
foster.exZh: 给孩子读书能培养他们对书的热爱。
foster.col: foster creativity 培养创造力；foster parents 养父母
foster.zh: v. 培养；促进；收养　adj. 寄养的

mn: in-（进入）+ duc（引导，同 introduce、produce）→ 把人引进去 → 诱使、导致
induce.ex: Nothing could induce me to take that job.
induce.exZh: 什么都不能诱使我接受那份工作。
induce.col: induce sb. to do 诱使某人做；stress-induced 压力引起的

mn: sub-（下面）+ stant（站，同 stand、stable）→ 下面站得住的实物 → 实质的 → 分量大的
substantial.ex: A substantial number of students work part-time.
substantial.exZh: 相当多的学生在做兼职。
substantial.col: a substantial amount/increase 大量/大幅增加
substantial.fam: substance n. 物质；substantially adv. 大大地
substantial.zh: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质的

mn: tra（=trans 穿过）+ ject（扔，同 project 投射、reject 拒绝）→ 扔出去穿过空中的路线 → 轨迹
trajectory.ex: The company is on an upward trajectory.
trajectory.exZh: 这家公司正处于上升轨道。

mn: en-（在……上）+ dors（背，同 dorsal 背部的）→ 在支票背面签名 →“背书”→ 认可、代言
endorse.ex: The plan was endorsed by the city council.
endorse.exZh: 该计划得到了市议会的认可。
endorse.col: endorse a candidate 支持候选人

mn: de-（去掉）+ fic（做，同 efficient 高效的）→ 做得不够、少了一块 → 不足、赤字
deficit.ex: The country has a large trade deficit.
deficit.col: budget deficit 预算赤字；trade deficit 贸易逆差

mn: com-（全部）+ pris（抓，同 prison 监狱、enterprise 企业）→ 把全部抓在里面 → 包括、组成
comprise.ex: The class comprises 30 students from ten countries.
comprise.exZh: 这个班由来自十个国家的 30 名学生组成。
comprise.col: be comprised of = consist of 由……组成

mn: con-（加强）+ strain（拉紧，同 strict 严格的、restrain 抑制）→ 绳子拉得紧紧的 → 限制
constrain.ex: Our research was constrained by a lack of funding.
constrain.exZh: 我们的研究受到资金不足的限制。

mn: as-（加强）+ sert（放入，同 insert 插入）→ 把观点硬插进讨论 → 断言、坚称
assert.ex: He asserted that he had done nothing wrong.
assert.exZh: 他断言自己没有做错任何事。
assert.col: assert oneself 坚持自己的主张
assert.fam: assertive adj. 自信果断的；assertion n. 断言
assert.zh: v. 断言；坚称；维护（权利）

mn: plaus（鼓掌，同 applause 掌声）+ -ible → 值得鼓掌认可的 → 似乎有道理的
plausible.ex: Her explanation sounds plausible, but I'm not sure it's true.
plausible.exZh: 她的解释听起来合理，但我不确定是不是真的。
plausible.col: a plausible explanation 合理的解释
plausible.zh: adj. 貌似合理的；可信的

mn: con（共同）+ front（前面）→ 面对面站在前面 → 面对、对抗
confront.ex: We must confront the problem instead of ignoring it.
confront.exZh: 我们必须正视问题，而不是回避它。
confront.col: be confronted with 面临；confront a problem 正视问题

mn: pre-（之前）+ limin（门槛，同 eliminate =“赶出门槛”）→ 跨进门槛之前的 → 初步的、预备的
preliminary.exZh: 初步结果看起来很有希望。
preliminary.col: preliminary results/stage 初步结果/阶段
preliminary.cf: 近义：tentative 暂定的（第 11 串）

mn: ambi-（两边，同 ambivalent 矛盾的）+ ig（驱动）→ 往两边都能走 → 模棱两可
“俺必够？”——到底够不够，说得含含糊糊
ambiguous.ex: The instructions were ambiguous, so everyone did something different.
ambiguous.exZh: 说明含糊不清，所以每个人做的都不一样。
ambiguous.col: an ambiguous answer 含糊的回答
ambiguous.cf: 反义：explicit 明确的（第 9 串）
ambiguous.zh: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊的

mn: 希腊语 skept（看、审视，和 scope 同源，如 telescope 望远镜）→ 凡事都要拿望远镜看清再信 → 怀疑的
skeptical.ex: Many experts are skeptical about the new diet.
skeptical.exZh: 许多专家对这种新饮食法持怀疑态度。
skeptical.col: be skeptical of/about 对……持怀疑态度
skeptical.fam: skeptic n. 怀疑者；skepticism n. 怀疑态度

mn: rig（僵硬，同 rigid 僵硬的）→ 一点不肯变通 → 严格的、严谨的
“瑞哥人死”——瑞哥做事严谨到让人崩溃
rigorous.ex: All new drugs must pass rigorous tests.
rigorous.exZh: 所有新药都必须通过严格测试。
rigorous.col: rigorous training/analysis 严格训练/严谨分析

mn: em-（在……中）+ pir（尝试，和 experiment 实验是近亲）→ 在试验中得来的 → 实证的
“硬劈了个”——光说理论不信，硬劈开一个看看 → 实证
empirical.ex: There is little empirical evidence to support the theory.
empirical.exZh: 几乎没有实证证据支持这一理论。
empirical.col: empirical evidence/study 实证证据/研究
empirical.zh: adj. 实证的；以观察或实验为依据的

mn: en（使）+ tail（尾巴）→ 一件事后面必然拖着一条尾巴 → 需要、牵涉
entail.ex: The job entails a lot of travel.
entail.exZh: 这份工作需要经常出差。
entail.col: entail risk 涉及风险；What does the job entail? 这份工作具体做什么？

mn: re-（回）+ frain（马笼头）→ 勒住缰绳往回拉 → 克制住
refrain.ex: Please refrain from smoking in the building.
refrain.col: refrain from doing 克制不做；请勿……
refrain.zh: v. 克制；避免　n. 副歌

mn: para（旁边）+ digm（展示）→ 放在旁边给大家照着学的样板 → 范例、范式
g 不发音，读作 /ˈpærədaɪm/，结尾像 dime（一角硬币）
paradigm.ex: The discovery led to a paradigm shift in physics.
paradigm.exZh: 这一发现带来了物理学的范式转变。

mn: vol（飞，同 volley 截击）→ 一会儿飞走一会儿飞回 → 易变的、易挥发的
“我了太凶”——我(vo)脾气了(la)不得，太(tile)易变
volatile.ex: Oil prices have been extremely volatile this year.
volatile.col: a volatile market 动荡的市场；a volatile temper 喜怒无常
volatile.cf: 相关：fluctuate 波动（第 11 串）
volatile.zh: adj. 易变的；动荡的；易挥发的

mn: lever（杠杆）← lev（举起，同 elevator 电梯）→ 以小博大 → 影响力、利用
leverage.ex: We should leverage our experience to enter new markets.
leverage.exZh: 我们应利用自身经验进入新市场。
leverage.col: leverage resources 利用资源；gain leverage 获得筹码
leverage.zh: n. 杠杆作用；影响力；筹码　v. 利用

mn: luc 像 lucky：运气好，钱哗哗来 → 利润丰厚的
“撸克拉踢”——撸下一克拉钻石还踢一脚，真有钱
lucrative.ex: She left a lucrative job to start her own business.
lucrative.exZh: 她辞去了收入丰厚的工作去创业。
lucrative.col: a lucrative business/deal 赚钱的生意
lucrative.zh: adj. 赚钱的；利润丰厚的

mn: in-（进入）+ cur（跑，同 current 水流、occur 发生）→ 一头跑进麻烦里 → 招致
incur.ex: The company incurred heavy losses last year.
incur.exZh: 公司去年遭受了重大损失。
incur.col: incur costs/debts/losses 产生费用/负债/损失
incur.zh: v. 招致；遭受；产生（费用）

mn: “阿伯收立特”——阿伯收着的老式随身听，早过时了
obsolete.exZh: 手机让寻呼机被淘汰了。

mn: “饿累极”——小偷声称：我饿极累极才偷的（但没证据）
新闻里一看到 allegedly（据称），就要在心里打个问号：说法未经证实
allege.ex: The report alleges that the company hid safety problems.
allege.exZh: 报告指称该公司隐瞒了安全问题。
allege.zh: v. 声称；指控（尚未证实）

mn: account（账）+ able → 能被拉出来算账的 → 要负责的
accountable.ex: Politicians should be held accountable for their decisions.
accountable.exZh: 政客应为自己的决定负责。
accountable.col: hold sb. accountable 追究某人责任
accountable.zh: adj. 负有责任的；需作解释的

mn: “米提给它”——灾民缺粮？提米给它 → 灾情减轻
miti（温和）→ 使变温和 → 缓和
mitigate.ex: Planting trees can help mitigate the effects of climate change.
mitigate.exZh: 植树有助于减轻气候变化的影响。
mitigate.col: mitigate the impact/risk 减轻影响/降低风险

mn: stag 像 stand / stay：一直站着不动 → 停滞的；stagnant water 一潭死水
stagnant.ex: Wages have remained stagnant for years.
stagnant.col: a stagnant economy 停滞的经济

mn: 拉丁语 deterior =“更差的”（结构像 inferior 更差的）→ 越来越差 → 恶化
“地铁里鹅瑞特”——地铁里挤进一只鹅，情况越来越糟
deteriorate.col: a deteriorating situation 不断恶化的局势
deteriorate.cf: 近义：exacerbate 使恶化（第 11 串，及物）

mn: dis-（不）+ par（相等，同 compare 比较、parity 平等）→ 不相等 → 差距
disparity.ex: There is a huge disparity between rich and poor.
disparity.col: income/regional disparity 收入/地区差距
disparity.cf: discrepancy 指数据、说法对不上（第 14 串）

mn: ex-（向外）+ plic（折叠，同 complicated 复杂的）→ 把折起来的展开 → 清清楚楚
反义 implicit 含蓄的：im-（向内）折起来 → 不说透
explicit.ex: The teacher gave explicit instructions about the exam.
explicit.exZh: 老师对考试给出了明确的说明。
explicit.zh: adj. 明确的；清楚的；露骨的

mn: prag（做，和 practice 实践同源）→ 重实际行动的 → 务实的
pragmatic.ex: We need a pragmatic solution, not a perfect one.
pragmatic.exZh: 我们需要务实的解决方案，而不是完美的。
pragmatic.col: a pragmatic approach 务实的方法
pragmatic.zh: adj. 务实的；实用主义的

mn: tang（触摸，同 contact 接触、tangent 切线）+ -ible → 摸得着的 → 有形的、切实的
tangible.ex: The training produced tangible results within weeks.
tangible.exZh: 培训在几周内就产生了实际效果。
tangible.col: tangible benefits/results 实际好处/成果

mn: hind（后面，同 behind）→ 有人把你往后拽 → 阻碍
hinder.ex: Bad weather hindered the rescue efforts.
hinder.exZh: 恶劣天气阻碍了救援工作。
hinder.col: hinder progress/development 阻碍进步/发展

mn: re-（回）+ sil（跳）→ 被压下去又跳回来 → 有弹性的、能复原的
“雷劈连它”——雷劈都连不倒它，弹回来了
resilient.ex: Children are often more resilient than adults think.
resilient.exZh: 孩子往往比大人想象的更有韧性。
resilient.col: a resilient economy 有韧性的经济
resilient.zh: adj. 有韧性的；能迅速恢复的

mn: pre-（在前）+ val（强，同 value、valid）→ 冲在前面占优势 → 盛行的
prevalent.ex: The disease is more prevalent among older people.
prevalent.exZh: 这种疾病在老年人中更普遍。
prevalent.col: be prevalent among/in 在……中普遍
prevalent.cf: 近义：pervasive（第 11 串）、ubiquitous（第 12 串）
prevalent.zh: adj. 普遍的；流行的；盛行的

mn: pro-（向前）+ vok（喊，同 voice、vocal）→ 冲到前面大喊 → 挑衅、激起
provoke.ex: His comments provoked an angry reaction.
provoke.exZh: 他的言论引起了愤怒的反应。
provoke.col: provoke anger/debate 激起愤怒/引发争论

mn: “阿比随意”——阿比做事全凭随意 → 任意的、武断的
arbiter（仲裁人）→ 全凭一个人说了算 → 武断
arbitrary.ex: The decision seemed arbitrary and unfair.
arbitrary.exZh: 这个决定显得武断且不公平。
arbitrary.col: an arbitrary decision 武断的决定
arbitrary.zh: adj. 任意的；武断的；专横的

mn: rational（理性的）+ e → 理性的依据 → 理由
rationale.ex: The rationale behind the new law is to protect children.
rationale.exZh: 新法律背后的理由是保护儿童。

mn: co-（共同）+ her（粘，第 5 串 inherent 里也有）→ 粘在一起 → 连贯的
coherent.ex: She wrote a clear and coherent essay.
coherent.exZh: 她写了一篇清晰连贯的文章。
coherent.col: a coherent argument 条理清楚的论证
coherent.zh: adj. 连贯的；条理清楚的

mn: al-（加强）+ lev（轻、举起，同 elevator 电梯）→ 把重担举起来、变轻 → 减轻
alleviate.ex: The medicine helped alleviate her pain.
alleviate.col: alleviate pain/poverty 缓解疼痛/减轻贫困

mn: under（在下面）+ mine（挖坑道）→ 在城墙根下偷偷挖 → 墙慢慢塌 → 暗中削弱
undermine.ex: Lack of sleep can undermine your health.
undermine.exZh: 缺乏睡眠会损害你的健康。
undermine.col: undermine confidence/trust 削弱信心/信任

mn: tent（尝试，同 attempt 尝试）→ 试一试的 → 试探性的
先搭个帐篷（tent）凑合住，不是永久房 → 暂定的
tentative.ex: We made a tentative plan to meet next Friday.
tentative.exZh: 我们初步打算下周五见面。
tentative.col: a tentative agreement 初步协议
tentative.zh: adj. 暂定的；试探性的；犹豫的

mn: “扭一点点”——意思只扭了一点点 → 细微差别
nuance.ex: Translators must understand every nuance of the text.
nuance.exZh: 译者必须理解原文的每一处细微差别。
nuance.zh: n. 细微差别；微妙之处

mn: flu（流，同 fluent 流利的、fluid 液体）→ 像水流一样一起一伏 → 波动
fluctuate.ex: Vegetable prices fluctuate with the seasons.
fluctuate.col: fluctuate between A and B 在 A 与 B 之间波动

mn: per-（贯穿）+ vas（走，同 invade 入侵、evade 逃避）→ 走遍每个角落 → 遍布的
pervasive.ex: Social media has a pervasive influence on young people.
pervasive.exZh: 社交媒体对年轻人的影响无处不在。
pervasive.col: a pervasive influence 广泛的影响
pervasive.zh: adj. 无处不在的；遍布的

mn: string（绳子）→ 用绳子勒得死死的 → 严格的
和 strict（严格的）同源：string-/strict- =“拉紧”
stringent.ex: The country has stringent laws against drunk driving.
stringent.exZh: 该国对酒驾有严格的法律。
stringent.col: stringent rules/standards 严格的规定/标准

mn: ex-（加强）+ acerb（苦、尖，和 acid 酸同源）→ 变得更苦更尖锐 → 加剧
“一个渣色杯”——一个渣男、一杯色酒，让事情更糟
exacerbate.col: exacerbate the problem 使问题恶化

mn: intr（在内，同 interior 内部、introduce）→ 从里面来的 → 内在的
反义 extrinsic 外在的（extr = 外）
intrinsic.ex: Learning has intrinsic value beyond getting a job.
intrinsic.exZh: 学习有超越找工作的内在价值。
intrinsic.col: intrinsic value/motivation 内在价值/内在动机

mn: ad-（去）+ vent（来，同 event 事件、adventure 冒险）→ 来到 → 到来、出现
advent.ex: The advent of the internet changed everything.
advent.exZh: 互联网的出现改变了一切。

mn: ubi 在拉丁语里是“在哪里”→ 在哪里都有 → 无处不在
开头的 u-bi 像 Uber：打开就有车，哪儿都有
ubiquitous.ex: Coffee shops are ubiquitous in big cities.
ubiquitous.exZh: 大城市里咖啡店随处可见。

mn: proli（后代，同 prolific 多产的）+ fer（带来，同 transfer）→ 不断生出后代 → 繁殖、激增
proliferate.ex: Fast-food restaurants have proliferated in recent years.

mn: three + live：一条命变三条命，活得红红火火 → 繁荣
thrive.ex: Some plants thrive in dry conditions.
thrive.exZh: 有些植物在干旱条件下长得很好。
thrive.col: thrive on sth. 因……而兴旺/乐在其中
thrive.cf: 反义：succumb 屈服、倒下（第 14 串）

mn: de-（向下）+ tri（磨，同 trite 陈腐的=磨旧了）→ 被慢慢磨损 → 有害的
“得吹门头”——台风一来，得把门头吹坏 → 有害
sus（=sub 在下面）+ cept（接受，同 accept、concept）→ 照单全收 → 易受影响的
susceptible.ex: Young children are more susceptible to infections.
susceptible.col: be susceptible to 易受……影响
susceptible.zh: adj. 易受影响的；易感染的

mn: “没题可漏死”——一道题都不漏，仔细得要死 → 一丝不苟
metic 原意“害怕”→ 怕出错，所以极其小心
meticulous.ex: She keeps meticulous records of her spending.
meticulous.exZh: 她一丝不苟地记录自己的开销。
meticulous.col: meticulous attention to detail 对细节一丝不苟
meticulous.zh: adj. 一丝不苟的；极仔细的

mn: af-（加强）+ flu（流，同 fluent）→ 钱哗哗流进来 → 富裕的
affluent.ex: They live in an affluent neighbourhood.
affluent.col: an affluent society 富裕社会
affluent.cf: 形近：adverse 不利的（第 14 串）

mn: com-（加强）+ plac（取悦，同 please）→ 把自己取悦得很满意 → 自满的
“看不累死”——自我感觉太好，看自己怎么都不累
complacent.ex: We can't afford to become complacent about safety.
complacent.exZh: 在安全问题上我们不能掉以轻心。
complacent.zh: adj. 自满的；自鸣得意的

mn: plum（=plumb 铅锤）→ 像铅锤一样直直坠下 → 暴跌
“扑了密”——一头扑下去，扑了个密不透风 → 暴跌
plummet.col: prices/sales plummet 价格/销量暴跌
plummet.cf: 反义：surge 激增（第 2 串）

mn: e-（出）+ rod（咬，同 rodent 啮齿动物）→ 像老鼠一样一口一口啃掉 → 侵蚀
erode.ex: The sea is slowly eroding the coastline.
erode.exZh: 海水正慢慢侵蚀海岸线。
erode.col: erode trust/confidence 削弱信任/信心

mn: “皆怕带死”——大家都怕它带来死亡 → 危及
jeopardize.ex: Missing classes could jeopardize your chances of passing.
jeopardize.exZh: 缺课可能危及你及格的机会。
jeopardize.col: jeopardize one's future/career 危及前途/事业
jeopardize.fam: jeopardy n. 危险（in jeopardy 处于危险中）

mn: feas（做，同 factory 工厂里的 fac）+ -ible → 能做成的 → 可行的
“飞着包”——用无人机飞着送包裹，现在可行了
feasible.ex: It is not feasible to finish the project in a week.
feasible.exZh: 一周内完成这个项目不可行。
feasible.col: a feasible plan 可行的方案；feasibility study 可行性研究

mn: in（里面）+ tric（花招，同 trick）→ 里面全是弯弯绕 → 错综复杂
intricate.ex: The carpet has an intricate pattern.
intricate.exZh: 这块地毯的图案错综复杂。
intricate.col: intricate design/details 精细的设计/细节
intricate.zh: adj. 错综复杂的；精细的

mn: ad-（朝向）+ vers（转，同 reverse 反转、version）→ 转过来跟你作对 → 不利的
adverse.ex: The drug may have adverse effects on some patients.
adverse.exZh: 这种药可能对一些病人产生不良反应。
adverse.col: adverse effects/weather 不良反应/恶劣天气
adverse.zh: adj. 不利的；有害的；相反的

mn: dis-（分开）+ crep（发出声响）→ 两个声音唱不到一块 → 不一致
“迪斯科乱拍子”——两人跳迪斯科，拍子对不上
discrepancy.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
discrepancy.exZh: 两份报告之间存在出入。
discrepancy.col: a discrepancy between A and B A 与 B 之间的出入

mn: con-（加强）+ spic（看，同 spectacle 景象、despise 看不起）→ 一眼就被看见 → 显眼的
conspicuous.ex: She felt conspicuous in her bright red coat.
conspicuous.exZh: 她穿着鲜红的大衣，觉得很显眼。
conspicuous.zh: adj. 显眼的；引人注目的

mn: 原义“长靠枕”：垫个靠枕把人撑起来 → 支撑、加强
“抱死它”——紧紧抱住它，给它撑腰
bolster.ex: The good news bolstered investors' confidence.
bolster.exZh: 好消息增强了投资者的信心。
bolster.col: bolster confidence/the economy 增强信心/提振经济
bolster.zh: v. 加强；支持；提振　n. 长枕

mn: ex-（出）+ empt（拿，同 redemption 赎回）→ 拿出去、不算在内 → 免除
exempt.ex: Food and medicine are exempt from the new tax.
exempt.col: be exempt from 免于……；tax-exempt 免税的
exempt.zh: adj. 被免除的　v. 免除

mn: suc（=sub 在下面）+ cumb（躺）→ 躺倒在下面 → 屈服、倒下
“色看”——一看到美色就屈服了（b 不发音）
succumb.ex: He finally succumbed to temptation and ate the cake.
succumb.exZh: 他最终抵不住诱惑，吃了蛋糕。
succumb.col: succumb to pressure/temptation 屈服于压力/诱惑
succumb.zh: v. 屈服；抵挡不住；死于（to）

mn: con-（加强）+ cede（走开、让，同 proceed）→ 让出路来 → 让步、勉强承认
“肯西的”——终于肯把西边的地让给你
concede.ex: He conceded that he had made a mistake.

stories.title: 市长的难题
stories.story: The new mayor faced a real dilemma. The city's old infrastructure was falling apart, but tax revenue was too low to fix it. Residents had a legitimate complaint, yet the council could not reach a consensus. When the repair plan was finally implemented, its effect on daily life was profound.
stories.storyZh: 新市长陷入了两难。城市的老旧基础设施正在崩坏，可税收太少，修不起。居民的抱怨合情合理，议会却迟迟达不成共识。修缮计划终于实施后，对日常生活的影响十分深远。

stories.title: 一家初创公司
stories.story: A small startup built a sophisticated app that disrupted the taxi industry. After a surge in users, prospective investors lined up at its door. Its robust growth soon offset the early losses, and customers happily embraced the new service.
stories.storyZh: 一家小型初创公司开发了一款精密的应用，颠覆了出租车行业。用户激增之后，潜在投资者排队上门。强劲的增长很快抵消了早期亏损，顾客也欣然接受了这项新服务。

stories.title: 法庭上
stories.story: The lawyer contended that the police had no warrant to search the house. Under close scrutiny, the evidence looked far less compelling. The judge, a woman of great integrity, deemed the search illegal, and newspapers depicted the trial as a victory for privacy.
stories.storyZh: 律师主张警方没有搜查令就搜了房子。经过仔细审查，证据远没有那么有说服力。正直的女法官认定这次搜查违法，报纸把这场审判描绘成隐私权的胜利。

stories.title: 绿色新政
stories.story: To curb air pollution, the government offered subsidies for solar panels. A new law mandated that factories report their emissions in a transparent way. Experts believe the plan is viable and can be sustained for decades, an unprecedented shift for the country.
stories.storyZh: 为了遏制空气污染，政府为太阳能板提供补贴。一项新法律强制要求工厂透明地报告排放。专家认为这个计划可行，能持续几十年——对这个国家来说是前所未有的转变。

stories.title: 一位好老师
stories.story: A prominent teacher believed that every child has an inherent curiosity. She fostered it with games instead of tests, which induced even shy students to speak up. Her method had a substantial effect on their career trajectories, and the school board later endorsed it.
stories.storyZh: 一位知名教师相信，每个孩子都有与生俱来的好奇心。她用游戏而不是考试来培养它，连害羞的学生都被引得开口发言。她的方法对学生们的职业轨迹产生了重大影响，后来得到了校董会的认可。

stories.title: 家庭账本
stories.story: Our family budget showed a deficit. Rent comprises half of our spending, which constrains everything else. My brother asserted that we could save money by cooking at home, which was a plausible idea. That night, we finally confronted the problem together.
stories.storyZh: 我们家的预算出现了赤字。房租占了开销的一半，其他一切都受到限制。哥哥断言在家做饭就能省钱，这想法挺有道理。那天晚上，我们终于一起正视这个问题。

stories.title: 一项新研究
stories.story: The preliminary results looked exciting, but the data were ambiguous. Skeptical reviewers asked for more rigorous, empirical tests, which would entail another year of work. Until then, the team refrained from claiming a new paradigm.
stories.storyZh: 初步结果令人兴奋，但数据模棱两可。持怀疑态度的审稿人要求做更严格的实证测试，这意味着还要再干一年。在那之前，团队克制住了宣称“新范式”的冲动。

stories.title: 交易员的陨落
stories.story: The stock market was volatile that year. A young trader used leverage to chase lucrative returns, but he incurred huge losses when his strategy became obsolete. Investors alleged that he had hidden the risks, and the firm was held accountable. New rules now aim to mitigate such risks.
stories.storyZh: 那一年股市剧烈波动。一位年轻交易员用杠杆追逐丰厚回报，策略过时后却蒙受巨亏。投资者指称他隐瞒了风险，公司被追究责任。如今的新规旨在降低这类风险。

stories.title: 小镇的冬天
stories.story: As the economy grew stagnant, conditions in the small town deteriorated, and the disparity between rich and poor widened. The mayor gave explicit instructions to help, and volunteers took a pragmatic approach: free hot meals that brought tangible relief. Icy roads hindered their work, but the town proved resilient.
stories.storyZh: 随着经济停滞，小镇的状况不断恶化，贫富差距拉大。镇长下达了明确的救助指示，志愿者采取了务实的做法：免费热饭，带来了实实在在的帮助。结冰的道路阻碍了工作，但小镇展现出了韧性。

stories.title: 一条谣言
stories.story: Rumours are prevalent online. One post provoked anger by claiming that the new school rule was arbitrary and had no rationale. In fact, the rule was clear and coherent, and it was designed to alleviate students' workload. The post simply undermined public trust.
stories.storyZh: 网上谣言很普遍。一条帖子声称新校规很武断、毫无道理，激起了众怒。事实上，这条规定清晰且条理分明，目的是减轻学生负担。那条帖子只是破坏了公众信任。

stories.title: 职场第一年
stories.story: In her first job, Lin made a tentative suggestion, but she missed the nuance of her boss's reply. Her mood fluctuated for weeks. A pervasive culture of criticism and stringent deadlines exacerbated the stress, yet her intrinsic love of the work kept her going.
stories.storyZh: 第一份工作里，林小心地提了个建议，却没听出老板回复里的微妙意味。她的情绪起伏了好几周。无处不在的批评文化和严苛的截止日期加剧了压力，但她对工作发自内心的热爱支撑她走了下去。

stories.title: 手机时代
stories.story: Since the advent of smartphones, screens have become ubiquitous, apps have proliferated, and tech companies thrive. Doctors warn that too much screen time is detrimental to sleep, and teenagers are especially susceptible. Even a meticulous designer I know admits that he checks his phone a hundred times a day.
stories.storyZh: 自从智能手机出现，屏幕无处不在，应用激增，科技公司欣欣向荣。医生警告，看屏幕太久有害睡眠，青少年尤其易受影响。就连我认识的一位一丝不苟的设计师也承认，他每天要看一百次手机。

stories.title: 老字号的转身
stories.story: For decades, the old restaurant served affluent customers and grew complacent. When delivery apps arrived, its sales plummeted and its reputation eroded. Rising rents jeopardized its future. Then the owners found a feasible solution: they turned their intricate family recipes into cooking classes.
stories.storyZh: 几十年来，这家老餐馆服务着富裕的顾客，渐渐变得自满。外卖应用兴起后，它的销量暴跌，名声也受损。不断上涨的房租危及它的未来。后来老板找到了一个可行的办法：把复杂精细的家传菜谱变成了烹饪课。

stories.title: 登山队
stories.story: The climbing team met adverse weather near the summit. One climber noticed a discrepancy between the map and the trail. Their bright orange jackets were conspicuous against the snow, which bolstered the rescuers' hopes. No one was exempt from exhaustion; two climbers nearly succumbed to the cold, and the leader finally conceded that they had to turn back.
stories.storyZh: 登山队在峰顶附近遭遇恶劣天气。一名队员发现地图和路线对不上。他们鲜橙色的外套在雪地里十分显眼，这让救援人员更有信心。没有人能免于精疲力竭；两名队员差点冻倒，队长最终承认必须折返。

articles.title: The Cat Who Ran for Mayor
articles.hook: 周一早上，帕德尔顿镇的人们醒来发现：镇长竞选里最受欢迎的候选人，是一只橘猫。它不会说话，却赢得了所有人。背后到底是谁在操纵？
paras: On a Monday morning in the small town of Puddleton, people woke up to a strange piece of news: the most popular candidate for mayor was a cat.
帕德尔顿小镇的一个周一早上，人们醒来就看到一条怪新闻：镇长竞选中最受欢迎的候选人，是一只猫。
His name was Sir Whiskers, a fat orange cat with one torn ear and the calm face of a philosopher.
它叫胡须爵士，一只胖胖的橘猫，一只耳朵缺了个口，脸上带着哲学家般的淡定。
Nobody knew who had signed him up.
没人知道是谁给它报的名。
The town had been in a dilemma for years.
小镇多年来一直左右为难。
Its infrastructure was a joke: the only bridge shook when a bicycle crossed it, and the streetlights worked only on Tuesdays.
基础设施简直是个笑话：唯一的一座桥，自行车一过就晃，路灯只在周二亮。
Tax revenue was falling, the town had a deficit the size of a small lake, and the two human candidates spent most of their time shouting at each other.
税收不断下降，财政赤字大得像个小湖，两位人类候选人则把大部分时间花在互相吼叫上。
So when a cat appeared on the ballot, many voters thought: honestly, why not?
所以当一只猫出现在选票上时，很多选民心想：说真的，为什么不行呢？
At first, Mayor Grumble refused to treat the cat as a legitimate candidate.
起初，格兰布尔镇长拒绝把这只猫当作合法的候选人。
"This is unprecedented!" he asserted on television.
“这是前所未有的！”他在电视上断言。
"A cat cannot implement a budget!"
“猫怎么可能执行预算！”
But his angry face only induced more people to support Sir Whiskers.
可他那张怒气冲冲的脸，只引得更多人支持胡须爵士。
Within a week, there was a surge of orange posters all over town.
一周之内，镇上的橘色海报猛增，到处都是。
They depicted the cat sitting on a pile of books, with a simple slogan: "I will not lie to you. I cannot talk."
海报上画着这只猫坐在一摞书上，配着一句简单的口号：“我不会骗你，因为我不会说话。”
The campaign was surprisingly sophisticated.
这场竞选出奇地专业。
Someone ran a transparent website that listed every cent the campaign received, so prospective donors could watch the money in real time.
有人运营了一个透明的网站，列出竞选收到的每一分钱，潜在的捐款人可以实时看到钱的去向。
A prominent local baker endorsed the cat and offered free fish-shaped bread to every voter.
当地一位有名的面包师公开支持这只猫，还给每位选民送免费的鱼形面包。
Young people embraced the idea at once; they said Sir Whiskers had an inherent honesty that no politician could fake.
年轻人立刻接受了这个主意；他们说胡须爵士有一种与生俱来的诚实，没有哪个政客装得出来。
Of course, the cat came under close scrutiny.
当然，这只猫也受到了严格审查。
Reporters followed him everywhere: to the fish market, to the library roof, and to a rubbish bin behind the police station, which they deemed "a worrying choice for a future leader."
记者到处跟着它：去鱼市场，上图书馆屋顶，还去了警察局后面的一个垃圾桶——记者们认为这是“未来领导人令人担忧的选择”。
One reporter even asked whether the police needed a warrant to search it.
一位记者甚至问，警察搜查那个垃圾桶需不需要搜查令。
Professor Hart, a skeptical scientist from the university, contended that the whole thing was a trick.
大学里一位持怀疑态度的科学家哈特教授声称，整件事就是个骗局。
"Cats do not have political views," she said.
“猫没有政治观点，”她说。
"The evidence for this so-called genius is ambiguous at best."
“所谓的天才，证据充其量也是模棱两可。”
To settle the matter, she designed a rigorous experiment.
为了把事情弄清楚，她设计了一个严格的实验。
It would entail three bowls, three budget plans and one very hungry cat.
实验需要三个碗、三份预算方案和一只非常饿的猫。
Each plan was placed under a bowl of fish.
每份方案都压在一碗鱼下面。
The preliminary results were shocking: Sir Whiskers ignored the fish, walked past two plans, and sat on the third, the only one that cut the mayor's salary and spent the money on the bridge.
初步结果令人震惊：胡须爵士没理那几碗鱼，走过两份方案，坐在了第三份上——唯一一份削减镇长工资、把钱花在修桥上的方案。
She repeated the test ten times.
她把测试重复了十次。
The cat chose the same plan every time.
猫每次都选同一份。
The empirical data were compelling, and Professor Hart, a woman of great integrity, did not hide them.
实证数据很有说服力，而哈特教授为人十分正直，没有隐瞒结果。
"I still refrain from calling it genius," she told the newspaper, "but this cat has better judgment than our council."
“我仍然不会称它为天才，”她对报社说，“但这只猫的判断力比我们的议会强。”
Her report had a profound effect.
她的报告产生了深远的影响。
Overnight, the town reached a rare consensus: whatever Sir Whiskers was, he deserved a chance.
一夜之间，小镇达成了少有的共识：不管胡须爵士是什么，它都值得一次机会。
Mayor Grumble decided to confront his rival face to face at the final debate.
格兰布尔镇长决定在最后一场辩论上和对手当面对质。
He spoke for forty minutes about growth and robust leadership.
他讲了四十分钟的经济增长和强有力的领导。
Sir Whiskers yawned, knocked the mayor's water glass off the table, and fell asleep.
胡须爵士打了个哈欠，把镇长的水杯扫到地上，然后睡着了。
The crowd went wild.
观众沸腾了。
It was the most honest response to a political speech they had ever seen.
这是他们见过的对政治演讲最诚实的回应。
Sir Whiskers won by a landslide.
胡须爵士以压倒性优势获胜。
Of course, he could not sign laws, so the new council comprised five humans who had to follow one simple rule: before any decision, they placed the plans in front of the cat.
当然，它不会签署法律，所以新议会由五个人类组成，他们要遵守一条简单的规定：做任何决定前，先把方案摆在猫面前。
The rule constrained the council in useful ways.
这条规定以一种有益的方式约束了议会。
It curbed long meetings, because the cat always left after ten minutes.
它遏制了冗长的会议，因为猫总是十分钟后就走。
It mandated short reports, because the cat only sat on short ones.
它强制要求报告要简短，因为猫只坐在短的报告上。
A year later, the bridge was fixed, a small subsidy helped local shops offset their losses, and the town's budget finally looked viable.
一年后，桥修好了，一小笔补贴帮本地商店抵消了亏损，小镇的预算终于显得可行了。
Journalists from around the world came to study this strange new paradigm of government.
世界各地的记者都来研究这种奇特的新型治理范式。
Could it be sustained?
这能持续下去吗？
Was it a plausible model for other towns?
这对其他小镇来说是可行的模式吗？
Experts argued, and the price of orange cats went up.
专家们争论不休，橘猫的价格也涨了。
The trajectory of Puddleton had changed, and a substantial number of tourists now came just to take photos with the mayor.
帕德尔顿的发展轨迹变了，现在有相当多的游客专程来和镇长合影。
Only one person knew the truth.
只有一个人知道真相。
Every night, eighty-year-old Mrs. Lin, who lived next to the town hall and had fostered more than thirty stray cats, rubbed a little fish oil on the plan she liked best.
每天晚上，住在镇政府隔壁、收养过三十多只流浪猫的八十岁林奶奶，都会在她最中意的那份方案上抹一点鱼油。
She had been a budget officer for forty years, and nobody had ever listened to her.
她当了四十年预算员，从来没人听过她的意见。
Now the whole town listened.
如今全镇都在听了。
The only thing the election disrupted was her bedtime, and she did not mind at all.
这场选举唯一打乱的是她的睡觉时间，而她一点也不介意。

articles.title: The Great Dumpling Heist
articles.hook: 暴风雨之夜，一份守了六十年的饺子秘方凭空消失。三个嫌疑人：富得流油的连锁店老板、炒币欠债的侄子、一台机器人厨师。八十岁的林奶奶拎着装猫的购物篮出马了……
paras: Every town has a secret, and Puddleton's secret was a dumpling recipe.
每个小镇都有一个秘密，帕德尔顿的秘密是一份饺子配方。
For sixty years, Golden Moon Dumplings had served the same dumplings, and the recipe was so intricate that only the owner, old Mr. Chen, knew all forty-one steps.
六十年来，金月饺子馆一直卖同一种饺子，配方复杂到只有老板陈老先生知道全部四十一个步骤。
Food bloggers called the dumplings "addictive."
美食博主说这饺子“会上瘾”。
Doctors called them "detrimental to your waistline."
医生说它“对腰围有害”。
Everyone ate them anyway.
反正大家照吃不误。
Then, on a stormy Friday night, the recipe disappeared.
然后，在一个暴风雨的周五夜晚，配方不见了。
The next morning, Mr. Chen stood in his kitchen, pale and shaking.
第二天早上，陈先生站在厨房里，脸色苍白，浑身发抖。
"Without the recipe," he said, "this shop will succumb in a month."
“没有配方，”他说，“这家店一个月就撑不住了。”
Sales would plummet, and the shop's reputation would erode.
销量会暴跌，店的名声会一点点被毁掉。
The loss jeopardized everything his family had built.
这次丢失危及他家打拼下来的一切。
The police were not much help.
警察帮不上什么忙。
The officer in charge was complacent and more interested in the free dumplings than in the case.
负责的警官很自满，比起案子，他对免费饺子更感兴趣。
He even said that Mr. Chen should be held accountable for leaving such a valuable recipe on a kitchen shelf.
他甚至说，陈先生把这么值钱的配方随手放在厨房架子上，责任应该由他自己承担。

So Mr. Chen called the one person in town whose talent was impossible to miss and whose reputation was conspicuous: Mrs. Lin, the eighty-year-old former budget officer who had secretly helped a cat become mayor.
于是陈先生打给了镇上本事最大、名气最响的那个人：林奶奶，那位八十岁的前预算员，曾经暗中帮一只猫当上了镇长。
She arrived ten minutes later with a notebook, a magnifying glass, and Sir Whiskers in a shopping basket.
十分钟后她就到了，带着一个笔记本、一个放大镜，购物篮里还装着胡须爵士。
Mrs. Lin was meticulous.
林奶奶一丝不苟。
She measured the footprints, counted the spoons, and noticed a small discrepancy: the back door was locked, but the window above the sink was open a few centimetres.
她量了脚印，数了勺子，还发现了一处小小的对不上：后门锁着，但水槽上方的窗户开了几厘米。
"Too small for a person," she said tentatively, "but let's not jump to conclusions."
“人钻不进来，”她试探着说，“不过我们先别急着下结论。”
There were three suspects, and each had a rationale for wanting the recipe.
有三个嫌疑人，每个人都有想要这份配方的理由。
The first was Victor Gold, the affluent owner of a dumpling chain.
第一个是维克多·戈尔德，一家饺子连锁店的富有老板。
His shops had proliferated so fast that they were now ubiquitous, but his dumplings tasted like wet paper.
他的店扩张得太快，如今随处可见，但他的饺子吃起来像湿纸。
The disparity between his wealth and the quality of his food was famous.
他的财富和他家饺子的质量之间的巨大差距，是出了名的。
He had tried for years to buy the recipe, and Mr. Chen's answer had always been explicit: "Never."
他多年来一直想买这份配方，陈先生的回答始终很明确：“休想。”
The second suspect was Mr. Chen's nephew, Kevin, who had lost a lot of money on volatile cryptocurrencies.
第二个嫌疑人是陈先生的侄子凯文，他在剧烈波动的加密货币上赔了很多钱。
He had used leverage, incurred huge debts, and was now looking for something lucrative to sell.
他加了杠杆，欠下巨债，现在正想找点值钱的东西卖。
The third was ChefBot 3000, a robot cook that Mr. Chen had bought last spring.
第三个是“厨师机器人 3000”，陈先生去年春天买的机器人厨师。
Since its advent, the human cooks in the kitchen had all felt a little obsolete.
自从它来了，厨房里的人类厨师都觉得自己有点要被淘汰了。
Kevin was the first to provoke Mrs. Lin.
凯文第一个来招惹林奶奶。
"You can't allege anything without proof," he said loudly.
“没有证据，你什么都不能指控，”他大声说。
"Your so-called investigation is completely arbitrary!"
“你这所谓的调查完全是瞎来！”
Mrs. Lin smiled.
林奶奶笑了。
People who shout too early, she believed, usually have something to hide; but she also knew that this belief could undermine a fair investigation, so she wrote it down and moved on.
她相信，太早嚷嚷的人往往有事要藏；但她也知道，这种想法会妨碍公正的调查，于是把它记下来，接着往下查。
Victor Gold was smoother.
维克多·戈尔德就圆滑多了。
He invited her to his office, offered her tea, and talked about "market realities" and "pragmatic solutions."
他请她去办公室，给她倒茶，大谈“市场现实”和“务实的解决方案”。
To "mitigate the damage," he even offered to buy Golden Moon at half price.
他甚至提出要“减少损失”，愿意半价收购金月饺子馆。
But Mrs. Lin had worked with numbers for forty years.
可林奶奶跟数字打了四十年交道。
She noticed that his company's profits had been stagnant for two years and that its debts were growing: the situation was deteriorating fast.
她注意到他公司的利润已经停滞两年，债务还在增加：形势正在迅速恶化。
"A man in that position," she thought, "might do something stupid. Or something clever."
“处在那种境地的人，”她想，“可能会干蠢事。也可能干聪明事。”
The interview with ChefBot 3000 was the strangest.
和“厨师机器人 3000”的问话最离奇。
Its answers were perfectly coherent but had no nuance at all.
它的回答完全连贯，却一点微妙之处都没有。
"Did you take the recipe?" "Negative. My intrinsic programming does not include stealing. Would you like some dumplings?"
“你拿了配方吗？”“否。我的内在程序不包括偷窃。您要来点饺子吗？”
Then it served her a plate.
然后它给她端上一盘。
They were terrible.
难吃极了。
Whatever the robot was, it did not have the recipe.
不管这机器人是什么来头，它肯定没有配方。
For three days, the pressure grew.
三天里，压力越来越大。
Rumours about the case became prevalent online, and the town's mood fluctuated between anger and panic.
关于这个案子的谣言在网上传得到处都是，镇上的情绪在愤怒和恐慌之间来回波动。
Heavy rain hindered the search, and old Mr. Chen, who was susceptible to stress, stopped sleeping.
大雨阻碍了搜寻，本来就容易紧张的陈老先生开始失眠。
Nothing anyone said could alleviate his fear.
谁说什么都缓解不了他的恐惧。
Then a stringent food-safety inspector, who had always disliked Mr. Chen, chose this moment to visit, which exacerbated everything.
偏偏这时，一位一向不喜欢陈先生、执法严苛的食品安全检查员上门检查，让一切雪上加霜。
The pervasive fear was that Golden Moon would close forever.
弥漫全镇的恐惧是：金月饺子馆要永远关门了。
On the fourth night, Mrs. Lin did something unusual: she did nothing.
第四天晚上，林奶奶做了一件不寻常的事：她什么都没做。
She needed tangible evidence, not theories, and watching the kitchen all night was the only feasible plan.
她需要实实在在的证据，而不是推理；整夜守着厨房，是唯一可行的办法。
So she sat in the dark with Sir Whiskers and waited.
于是她和胡须爵士坐在黑暗中等着。
At midnight, something small and fast came through the open window.
午夜时分，一个又小又快的东西从开着的窗户钻了进来。
It was a squirrel.
是一只松鼠。
It ran straight to a loose brick behind the oven, pulled out a folded piece of paper, and began to chew it.
它径直跑到烤炉后面一块松动的砖那里，拽出一张折起来的纸，开始啃。
Sir Whiskers, who was usually too fat to chase anything, moved faster than anyone had ever seen.
平时胖得什么都懒得追的胡须爵士，动作快得前所未见。
In two seconds the squirrel was gone, and the recipe lay on the floor, wet but readable.
两秒钟后松鼠就跑没影了，配方落在地上，湿了，但还看得清。
The mystery was simple in the end.
谜底最后很简单。
On the night of the storm, the wind had blown the recipe off the shelf and behind the loose brick, where a squirrel had been storing food all winter.
暴风雨那晚，风把配方从架子上吹落，掉进了那块松动的砖后面——一只松鼠整个冬天都在那里囤粮。
In adverse weather, the recipe had simply fallen into the smallest bank in the world.
恶劣天气里，配方就这么掉进了世界上最小的银行。
The discovery bolstered Mrs. Lin's reputation even further.
这次发现让林奶奶的名声更响了。
Nobody had stolen anything.
其实没有人偷过任何东西。
Kevin conceded that he had shouted too much and promised to stay away from cryptocurrency.
凯文承认自己嚷嚷得太多，保证再也不碰加密货币。
Victor Gold, to everyone's surprise, admitted that his dumplings were terrible and asked Mr. Chen for cooking lessons.
出乎所有人意料，维克多·戈尔德承认自己的饺子难吃，还向陈先生请教厨艺。
The food-safety inspector, red in the face, declared the squirrel exempt from all kitchen rules.
那位食品安全检查员红着脸宣布：松鼠不受任何厨房规定约束。
Golden Moon reopened the next week, and the whole town lined up at the door.
金月饺子馆第二周重新开张，全镇的人都在门口排起了长队。
Puddleton had proved resilient once again, and the shop began to thrive like never before, partly thanks to a new item on the menu: the Squirrel Special, with walnuts.
帕德尔顿又一次证明了自己的韧性，饺子馆生意空前红火，部分要归功于菜单上的新品：松鼠特供，加核桃。
As for Sir Whiskers, he received free dumplings for life, which every doctor in town agreed was bad for his weight and wonderful for his mood.
至于胡须爵士，它获得了终身免费饺子——镇上每位医生都认为，这对它的体重很糟糕，对它的心情好极了。
